items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No code change was made. All the work happened in throwaway `python3 -c` one-liners, and no script was left in /app to judge.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: No files were written apart from the output. The project asked for a re-runnable decrypt script plus an extraction step, but none was left behind. That is a process gap, not a code change to grade.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No code to judge. In the ad-hoc commands, XOR 0x42 is used with no derivation in code (`bytes([b ^ 0x42 for b in orig])`), and paths are hardcoded to /tmp backup files.

items.name: Recovery method is principled
items.evidence: The key was confirmed against a leftover decrypted file (`Matches dec exact? True`), not derived from the magic. The agent still checked magic 0x377f0682, header checksum and all 4 frame checksums/salts (`Valid=True`). It let SQLite replay the WAL and verified count=11. No integrity_check was run.

items.name: Original evidence preserved before in-place repair
items.name_zh: 原地修复前保留原始文件
items.evidence: The agent made no backup of its own. It relied on the existing /tmp/db_recovery_backup/*.orig files and overwrote /app/main.db-wal with the decrypted bytes. It tested the read-write checkpoint on /tmp copies (step 21) and opened the database with mode=ro for extraction, so it lost nothing in practice.
